opportunities.title: Authors' Contingency Fund
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Professional authors resident in the UK or British citizens (fiction writers, illustrators, literary translators, scriptwriters, poets, journalists and others) for whom author-related activities make up a substantial amount of annual income. Not open to editors, copywriters, salaried journalists, or authors at the start of their careers. SoA membership not required. Repeat applicants must wait four calendar years since their last grant.
opportunities.summary: Hardship grants for authors in financial difficulty. Offers small, short-term grants to established professional writers in moments of crisis to help them return to normal working practice. Can be used for lost income, project shortfalls, illness impact, domestic upheaval, or one-off expenses like a new boiler or laptop.

opportunities.title: Authors' Foundation
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Writers who have been previously published or have a contract for their project with a commercial UK or Irish publisher. For book projects: commissioned by a commercial UK/Irish publisher, or have had at least one book published commercially by a UK/Irish publisher with strong likelihood next book will be published. For scripts: previously professionally performed or under contract. Hybrid/self-published not eligible; non-contributory contracts required. Successful applicants must wait four years before re-applying.
opportunities.summary: Grants to help develop a work-in-progress. Accepts submissions for fiction, non-fiction, poetry and script projects, funding research, travel or other general expenditure. Applicants are automatically considered for associated awards (Eric Ambler, Taner Baybars, John Brooks, Antonia Fraser, Arthur Welton, Great Britain Sasakawa).

opportunities.title: K Blundell Trust
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be British by birth and currently resident in the UK, under the age of 40 on Sunday 1 March 2026, and have a previous work (of which they are the sole author) published with a commercial UK publisher. Hybrid/self-published not eligible. Cannot apply to both K Blundell Trust and Authors' Foundation in the same calendar year.
opportunities.summary: Work-in-progress grants for British authors under 40 whose work aims to increase social awareness. Accepts fiction, non-fiction, poetry and script projects. The fund has now closed and will re-open for applications in 2027.

opportunities.title: Society of Authors' Access Fund
opportunities.eligibility_summary: All authors who create work for publication, broadcast or performance. Open to UK and Irish residents and British and Irish citizens. Membership not required but must meet SoA membership criteria. One grant per calendar year; preference to those who have not received funds previously.
opportunities.summary: Grants for travel, subsistence, childcare or access needs for events, residencies, and retreats. The fund is currently closed for applications and is expected to re-open for applications in 2027.

opportunities.title: Strachey Trust Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to all authors (per SoA Full Membership criteria, though membership is not required) who are UK resident or British citizens, working on a specific full-length literary project with strong likelihood of publication. One application per calendar year; successful applicants must wait four years before re-applying.
opportunities.summary: Grants to enable authors to travel to a UK or Republic of Ireland archive or collection to research manuscript material for a specific full-length literary project with strong likelihood of publication. Can cover travel, accommodation, subsistence, childcare/carer support, companion costs, access needs, and copyright permission costs.
